decisions.reason: The original only-if clause did not supply a sufficient defining condition. Replaced it with a precise uniform criterion and separated pathwise, expected, almost-sure and stated-confidence modes; the base bound uses the matching mode. Static, dynamic, interval and stochastic regret formulas, finite attainment and integrability requirements remain unchanged. Hazan §10.2.1 and Daniely et al. §1.1 were read; the latter explicitly uses expectation for randomized protocols. No algorithm-existence assertion or choice principle is used.

F1 incorrectly attributed fixed round losses and choices to the general protocol, whose Definition expressly allows losses chosen after the action. Corrected F1 to distinguish fixed horizon/action set from choice-before-observation timing and environment-dependent loss timing. This is nonfatal: the example itself fixes all losses and choices explicitly. Direct calculation gives static regret 3/2-1=1/2, dynamic regret 3/2, path length 1+1+1=3, and interval regrets (1/2,1/2,1/2,0,0,1/2). All minima are finite and attained; no choice axiom or strong-adaptivity guarantee is used. Example description and all proof steps remain unchanged.

F2 wrongly credited the regret definition with defining arm counts, whereas the finite-arm lemma explicitly defines N_i(T) as the sum of selected-arm indicators. Added that lemma as the exact supplier of the count clause and added its F2 citation contract; existing deps already include it. The error is nonfatal because the count definition is locally available and all arithmetic is sound. On the equiprobable two-point space Y_1 has P_2 law, mean 1/2, and both required event identities hold for the trivial pre-reward history. Means 3/4 and 1/2 give pseudo-regret 1/4, counts (0,1), realized reward regret values 3/4 and -1/4, expectation 1/4 and weighted expected-count sum 1/4. No unplayed reward or extra independence is assumed. Example description and proof steps remain unchanged.

No AC or existence assertion is added.

The repaired F1 faithfully permits model-dependent loss timing while retaining choice-before-observation. Recomputed static regret 1/2, dynamic regret 3/2, path length 3, and all six interval regrets with attained minima. The Example and Verification steps are unchanged; the owning contract quote, precheck and rendering pass.

The repaired F2 attributes indicator-sum arm counts to the finite-arm lemma and regret formulas to the regret definition. Checked both fixed-law and conditional-mean identities on the trivial history, counts (0,1), means (3/4,1/2), and pseudo-regret, expected reward regret and weighted-count sum all equal to 1/4. The Example and proof steps are unchanged; contract and focused checks pass.
